clue.text: Party's rejected a constituent for boozy tipples

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for the party's is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party, so the plural (written with the apostrophe) gives DOS

explanation.surface: A political party throws out one of its own voters over a habit of heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political and 'constituent' looks like a voter; in fact a do is a party, and the constituent is a mixer in a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is the mixer added to whisky or other spirits, so it is one ingredient of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Shelves in which American lifted forks out

indicators.note: in which says the next piece is placed within the one just named

parts.note: to fork out money is to spend it

explanation.surface: Someone describes shelving in which an American raised the cutlery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' tempts a reversal in a down clue, but nothing turns round here; it only adds to the picture of raised forks.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to put it on hold, which is to suspend it; both are verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Dull gathering Indian city stages, finally revealing plans

indicators.note: gathering means collecting something inside, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: dim means dull, as of light or wits
Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word stages

explanation.surface: A dreary meeting in an Indian city puts on shows that eventually disclose its schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagrams are drawings laid out to show how something is arranged, which is what plans of a building are.

clue.text: In aviators, undergoing turbulence leads to changes

indicators.note: turbulence shakes things about, so the letters of the fodder are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Pilots in a bumpy flight find that their leaders keep switching.
explanation.definitionFit: Variations are alterations or departures from a norm, a close synonym for changes as a plural noun.

clue.text: Issued an emblem of England

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
the red rose is the national flower of England

explanation.surface: Someone handed out a badge showing England's flower.
explanation.definitionFit: When something issued from a place it came forth or emerged, the sense of the past tense verb here.

clue.text: One is patron for organisation — time is of the essence

parts.note: one is, said by the speaker of themself, is I'm

indicators.note: needing organisation means the letters of patron are to be arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A sponsor stands up for a group, insisting that timing matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time is of the essence' reads as one stock phrase, but 'time' gives T and only 'of the essence' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of the essence is vital or crucial, the core of the matter, hence significant.

clue.text: Book about Putin's cash likely to cause ructions

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a tome is a large book
the rouble is the currency of Russia, which Putin leads

explanation.surface: A book exposing the Russian president's money is bound to stir up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something troublesome causes difficulty or disturbance, so it is apt to provoke rows.

clue.text: Gold US soldier should divide in beginning

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: dividing a word means splitting it, so the soldier is placed in the middle of it

parts.note: GI is the familiar name for an American soldier

explanation.surface: Gold should be shared among American troops at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The origin of anything is where it starts, so the noun beginning is a synonym.

clue.text: Say Trotter's around, one could go downhill fast

indicators.note: around signals turning the combined letters round to read the other way

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means when introducing an instance
Del Boy Trotter is the wheeler-dealer of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses, so Trotter's is Del's

explanation.surface: A man called Trotter is said to be nearby, perhaps a horse that could gallop down a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy Trotter is the market trader in the British TV comedy Only Fools and Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge is a sled ridden over snow, a vehicle that races down slopes.

clue.text: Did butterfly perhaps bring about gaping mouths?

indicators.note: bring about is taken literally as turning something about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: maws are the open jaws or mouths of animals

explanation.surface: A question whether a butterfly could make jaws fall open in wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butterfly' looks like the insect; it is the swimming stroke, an example indicated by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfly is a swimming stroke, so doing it in the past is an example of having taken a swim.

clue.text: Caught by love, married before engagement to get accommodation

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
an engagement is a promise or pledge, as of marriage

explanation.surface: Someone smitten and wed before they were engaged has had to make room for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching an accommodation means coming to a settlement in which each side gives ground.

clue.text: Pain coming from headgear, a check-up unveiled

indicators.note: coming from says the letters emerge out of the words that follow
unveiled means exposed, the letters revealed inside the words around them

explanation.surface: A headache caused by a hat is revealed at a medical examination.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a specific sort of pain, an ache inside the ear, so pain is a broader term for it.

clue.text: Facility being new in bay, northern relative's trapped inside

indicators.note: in places the new letter within the word for a bay

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

indicators.note: trapped inside means held within, so the abbreviation goes inside the relative

parts.note: a niece is a relative; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A new amenity in a bay has a northern relative stuck inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a convenience is also a public toilet, which suits 'Facility' as a polite euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: A convenience is an amenity or useful facility, and in British usage a public lavatory.

clue.text: Hood maybe involving bishop with grand larceny

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the bishop goes inside

parts.note: Robin Hood is the outlaw of English legend; the first name is what Hood suggests
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
G stands for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Robin Hood, perhaps with a bishop as accomplice, is involved in a major theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal name for theft, so taking property without consent is the shared sense.

clue.text: Review after seeing 'Devil and Saint' show

indicators.note: after means the review piece comes later than the devil and saint pieces

parts.note: a demon is a devil
to rate something is to assess or review it

explanation.surface: A critic writes a notice after watching a play called 'Devil and Saint'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like the noun the critic saw; it is the verb, to prove.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate is to prove or display something, which is what the verb show means.

clue.text: So the umpire wants product of mine?

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, is an umpire
ore is the rock extracted from a mine

explanation.surface: An official at a match wonders aloud whether a mine's output is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce a consequence, as in 'it rained; hence we stayed in', so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Person shopping me should be arrested by order of courts

indicators.note: being arrested means being held, so the word me is held inside the other letters
putting letters in a new order means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A shopper is told they should be detained by a court order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order of' signals the anagram of the courts' letters, and 'should be arrested by' puts the speaker's word inside the result, near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer is one who buys goods in a store, a shopper.

clue.text: Bank holds little European money of late

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the coin sits inside the other word

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
a cent is a hundredth of a euro, a small coin

explanation.surface: A bank has been keeping a small amount of euros lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like the noun; it is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: Of late means in the recent past, not long ago, an adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Choose twisted or clever end with a shock?

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so the two letters of the word or swap places

parts.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd, as in a cute move

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pick between a contorted plot and a clever one, ending with a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a playful definition: to end with a shock is to kill by electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: To electrocute is to kill by electric current, a death brought about by a jolt.

clue.text: Terrible automatic reaction after picking up newspaper

indicators.note: picking up means collecting, so the reaction takes the newspaper within it

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch or habitual reaction
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone has a dreadful knee-jerk response after collecting the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tragic is disastrous or calamitous, a synonym for dreadful in the sense of grievous.

clue.text: What's coming up on and off from one exec rocks TV

indicators.note: coming up, in a down clue, means the letters are read from bottom to top
on and off means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A question about what will soon be broadcast, judging by one executive who shakes television up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on and off' takes NEERCS from 'one exec rocks'; 'coming up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen is the display of a television, and by extension television as a medium, as in stars of the screen.

clue.text: Lie and refuse to see Republican ousting Democrat

indicators.note: ousting means driving out, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: to decline is to refuse

explanation.surface: A politician lies and won't see the opposition after a Republican unseats a Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' looks like a falsehood; it is the verb of lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean back or lie down, so it fits lie as a verb of rest.

clue.text: Herb tea's brewed, take in the air

indicators.note: brewed means mixed and steeped, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A herbal infusion is made, and the drinker steps outside for fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe is to draw air into the lungs, which is what taking in air means.

clue.text: Writer's accepted as essential

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the word as goes inside

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: An author's work has been taken on as indispensable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author; it is a Bic, the brand of ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something basic is fundamental or elementary, the core sense of essential as an adjective.

clue.text: Common uniform, wearing stockings in see-through construction

parts.note: a green is a common, a shared village grass area

indicators.note: wearing means having something on, so the stockings go round the letter

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An ordinary uniform worn with stockings in a transparent building.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhouse is a glass building for growing plants, so you can see right through it.

clue.text: Neglect to put about I'm making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the letters are read backwards
putting a word about another means wrapping it around, so the first goes outside

explanation.surface: An entertainer says they are ignoring the fuss about their return to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put about' is the container signal and 'making a comeback' turns the whole result round; 'about' looks like 'concerning' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to leave something out or fail to do it, which is what the verb neglect means.

clue.text: Enforce reforms by November church synod?

indicators.note: reforms means forms again, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: N is November in the NATO alphabet
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church council in November imposes changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a synod as one example of a formal meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church leaders, an example of a formal meeting.

clue.text: Something often in wood that bears nosh

definitions.text: Something often in wood that bears nosh

parts.words: Something often in wood that bears nosh
parts.note: the picture of a forest bear eating is false: the thing is often made of wood and carries food

explanation.surface: A creature in the forest that is a bear, eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wood' suggests a forest and 'bears' the animal; here wood is the material and bears means carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat board, often wooden, carries food and drink to the table, which is what nosh means: grub.
